sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(o.discount_amount), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS net_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-03-01 00:00:00' AND o.ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-04-01 00:00:00'
assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total gross sales (quantity * unit_price) minus discounts and refunds for orders placed in March 2026.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(order_total), 2) AS aov FROM (SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - COALESCE(o.discount_amount, 0) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.payment_method ILIKE '%card%' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.discount_amount)
assumptions: Average order value (AOV) is calculated per completed order as total item price minus discount, filtered for payment methods containing 'card'.
Orders table has a status column where 'completed' indicates valid orders, though filtering by status was not explicitly requested, AOV typically considers completed orders.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.ordered_at >= (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) - INTERVAL '30 days' FROM orders)
assumptions: Last 30 days is relative to the maximum ordered_at timestamp present in the orders table.
Completed orders are identified by status = 'completed'.

sql: SELECT count(*) AS new_customers FROM customers WHERE signup_at >= date_trunc('month', current_date - INTERVAL '1 month') AND signup_at < date_trunc('month', current_date)
assumptions: Last month is defined relative to the current system date using date_trunc('month', current_date - INTERVAL '1 month').

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 4) AS return_rate FROM orders o LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.ordered_at >= (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) - INTERVAL 90 DAY FROM orders) AND o.status != 'cancelled'
assumptions: Last 90 days is calculated relative to the maximum ordered_at timestamp in the orders table.
Return rate is defined as the fraction of orders that received at least one refund over the total number of orders in the period.
Cancelled orders are included or excluded depending on standard practice, assuming all non-cancelled orders or all orders are considered. Let's assume all orders in that time window.

sql: SELECT round(cast(sum(case when status = 'cancelled' then 1 else 0 end) as double) / count(*), 4) as cancellation_rate FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= date_trunc('month', current_date)
assumptions: Cancellation rate is defined as the number of cancelled orders divided by total orders placed in the current calendar month.
Current month is determined using date_trunc('month', current_date).

sql: SELECT count(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-02-09 00:00:00' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-02-10 00:00:00'
assumptions: Dates refer to the UTC timezone or stored timestamp values directly.

sql: SELECT count(order_id) AS completed_orders_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-05-01 00:00:00' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-06-01 00:00:00'
assumptions: May 2026 refers to the period from 2026-05-01 00:00:00 to 2026-05-31 23:59:59 inclusive.

sql: SELECT SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS gmv FROM order_items JOIN orders ON order_items.order_id = orders.order_id WHERE orders.ordered_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '60 days' AND orders.status <> 'cancelled'
assumptions: GMV is calculated as the sum of quantity multiplied by unit_price for all order items in non-cancelled orders placed within the last 60 days from current time.
The term 'last 60 days' uses NOW() as the reference point.

sql: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS lifetime_value FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = 2296 AND o.status != 'cancelled'
assumptions: Lifetime value is calculated as total revenue from non-cancelled orders minus refunds for customer 2296.
Revenue per order item is quantity multiplied by unit_price.

sql: SELECT count(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT c.customer_id, sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - coalesce(o.discount_amount, 0)) AS ltv FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - coalesce(o.discount_amount, 0)) > 15000) AS sub
assumptions: Lifetime value is calculated as the sum of (quantity * unit_price - discount_amount) across all non-cancelled orders per customer
Currencies are assumed to be consistent across the database and the query value of 15000 directly applies to the stored amounts

sql: WITH customer_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id), filtered_customers AS (SELECT customer_id, CASE WHEN completed_orders > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_repeat FROM customer_orders WHERE completed_orders >= 1) SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(is_repeat) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*), 4) AS repeat_fraction FROM filtered_customers
assumptions: Completed order status is represented by status = 'completed' in the orders table.
A repeat customer is defined as a customer with more than one completed order.

sql: SELECT acquisition_channel, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY acquisition_channel ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: New customers refer to all rows in the customers table.

sql: SELECT payment_method, ROUND(AVG(order_total), 2) AS aov FROM (SELECT o.order_id, o.payment_method, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - COALESCE(o.discount_amount, 0) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.payment_method, o.discount_amount) GROUP BY payment_method
assumptions: Order value is defined as the sum of (quantity * unit_price) of all items in the order minus the discount amount.

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN category = 'electronics' THEN quantity * unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / SUM(quantity * unit_price), 4) AS electronics_gmv_share FROM order_items
assumptions: GMV is calculated as the sum of quantity * unit_price from order_items.

sql: SELECT c.city AS city, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(o.discount_amount), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS net_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' AND o.ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2026-09-01 00:00:00' AND o.ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.city
assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total gross sales (quantity * unit_price) minus discounts and refunds for orders placed in September 2026, grouped by customer city.

sql: WITH first_completed_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.signup_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata' AS signup_ist, MIN(o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata') AS first_order_ist FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.signup_at) SELECT ROUND(AVG(DATE_PART('epoch', first_order_ist - signup_ist) / 86400), 2) AS avg_days_to_first_order FROM first_completed_orders
assumptions: Completed orders are identified by status = 'completed'
Timestamps are stored in UTC and converted to IST (Asia/Kolkata) using AT TIME ZONE
Difference in days between timestamps is calculated via epoch seconds divided by 86400

sql: WITH customer_spend AS (SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS total_spend FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status != 'cancelled' LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS zero_ltv_customers FROM customer_spend WHERE total_spend = 0
assumptions: Lifetime value is calculated as the sum of order item quantities multiplied by unit prices for all non-cancelled orders.
Customers with no orders or whose orders all have a total value of zero (or are cancelled) have a lifetime value of zero.

sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS returned_orders_with_refund FROM orders o JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.status = 'returned'
assumptions: A returned order is defined as an order where status = 'returned' in the orders table.
Having a refund record means there is at least one matching entry in the refunds table.
